Mantel and partial Mantel tests

Source: R/mantel.R
beta_mantel.Rd

beta_mantel() tests whether two distance matrices are correlated, for example community dissimilarity and elevational or geographic distance, with the Mantel test (Mantel 1967). With z, it gives the partial Mantel test of x and y controlling for z (Smouse et al. 1986). Significance comes from permuting the sites of x (vegan's vegan::mantel() and vegan::mantel.partial()).

Pairs of sites are not independent, so do not test distance-decay relationships with ordinary regression p-values; use this test instead. With few sites, use permutations = "exact" to enumerate every ordering of the sites (n!; 5,040 for 7 sites); the p-value is then exact.

alternative sets the tail: "greater" (the default) tests for a positive correlation, "less" for a negative one (for example similarity decreasing with distance), "two.sided" for either.

Usage

beta_mantel(
  x,
  y,
  z = NULL,
  method = c("spearman", "pearson", "kendall"),
  permutations = 9999,
  alternative = c("greater", "less", "two.sided"),
  strata = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

x, y, z

Distance matrices: dist objects (such as the result of beta_dist()), square matrices, or, for y and z, a numeric vector of site values (such as elevation), from which Euclidean distances are computed. All must describe the same sites in the same order; when they carry labels, the labels are matched.

method

Correlation: "spearman" (default), "pearson" or "kendall".

permutations

Number of permutations, or "exact".

alternative

"greater", "less" or "two.sided".

strata

Optional grouping of sites within which permutations are restricted.

seed

Optional random seed.

Value

A one-row tibble with statistic (the Mantel r), p.value, alternative, permutations, exact, method and partial.

References

Mantel, N. (1967). The detection of disease clustering and a generalized regression approach. Cancer Research, 27, 209-220.

Smouse, P. E., Long, J. C. and Sokal, R. R. (1986). Multiple regression and correlation extensions of the Mantel test of matrix correspondence. Systematic Zoology, 35, 627-632.

Examples

wet <- dplyr::filter(png_ants, season == "wet")
d_beta <- beta_dist(beta_pair(wet), "turnover")
elev <- dplyr::distinct(wet, site, elevation)
beta_mantel(d_beta, stats::setNames(elev$elevation, elev$site),
  permutations = "exact"
)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   statistic p.value alternative permutations exact method   partial
#>       <dbl>   <dbl> <chr>              <int> <lgl> <chr>    <lgl>  
#> 1     0.848  0.0167 greater              119 TRUE  spearman FALSE
